title: Microsoft Purview Audit: what the unified audit log records, how long it keeps it and what it costs
summary: The documented audit behaviour, licensing, retention limits and control paths are supported by Microsoft sources. The page correctly reports conflicting Microsoft guidance on AI audit billing and Dataverse retention rather than choosing one account.

claims.claim: The unified audit log records user and administrator operations across Microsoft services in a searchable store.
claims.quote: Your organization's unified audit log captures, records, and retains thousands of user and admin operations performed in dozens of Microsoft services and solutions.

claims.claim: An audited activity generates an audit record.
claims.quote: When a user or admin performs an audited activity, the system generates an audit record and stores it in the audit log for your organization.

claims.claim: Administrators can search audit records in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Use the Audit log search tool in the portal to search for audit records.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog in Exchange Online PowerShell searches the unified audit log.
claims.quote: You can also use the **Search-UnifiedAuditLog** cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell (the underlying cmdlet for the search tool) to search for audit events or to use in a script.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph supports programmatic audit searches.
claims.quote: allows you to programmatically access the audit search experience through Microsoft Graph.

claims.claim: The audit solutions have Standard and Premium tiers.
claims.quote: The following table compares the key capabilities available in Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium). Audit (Premium) includes all Audit (Standard) functionality.

claims.claim: Audit Standard is enabled by default for organizations with the appropriate subscription, subject to the exceptions explained later.
claims.quote: Audit (Standard) is enabled by default for all organizations with the appropriate subscription.

claims.claim: Audit Standard retains records for 180 days.
claims.quote: In Audit (Standard), the system retains records for 180 days, which means you can search for activities that occurred within the past six months.

claims.claim: Audit Premium adds audit log retention policies.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) builds on the capabilities of Audit (Standard) by providing audit log retention policies

claims.claim: Audit Premium supports retention up to one year without the ten-year add-on.
claims.quote: Create customized audit log retention policies to retain audit records for longer periods, up to one year (and up to 10 years for users with the required add-on license).

claims.where: What it is; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Retention up to ten years requires an additional user add-on license.
claims.quote: a user must be assigned a 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license to retain their audit records for 10 years.

claims.claim: Audit Premium adds intelligent insights.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) intelligent insights

claims.claim: Audit Premium provides higher Office 365 Management Activity API bandwidth.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) includes higher bandwidth access to the Office 365 Management Activity API, which provides faster access to audit data.

claims.claim: Dataverse auditing is configured at environment, table and column levels.
claims.quote: You can configure auditing at three levels: environment, table, and column. First, turn on auditing at the environment level. To log data changes in a table, turn on auditing for the table and for the column.

claims.claim: Dataverse user access or activity logging is sent to Purview for production environments only.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Retention follows the user's licence
claims.claim: Searchable retention depends on the license assigned to the user performing the activity.
claims.quote: The length of time that an audit record is retained (and searchable in the audit log) depends on your Office 365 or Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription, and specifically the type of the license that is assigned to specific users.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: Auditing is not enabled by default for Business Basic, Business Standard and Business Premium licenses.
claims.quote: Auditing isn't enabled by default for [Small and Medium Business (SMB) licenses](https://adoption.microsoft.com/small-and-medium-business/), including Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Business Standard, and Business Premium.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: Unmanaged tenants using enterprise license free trials must manually enable auditing.
claims.quote: Additionally, unmanaged tenants that use free trials of enterprise licenses don't have auditing enabled by default. In both these cases, you must manually enable auditing for your organization.

claims.claim: Purview audit searches return no results when auditing is turned off.
claims.quote: When you turn off auditing, searches of the audit log in Microsoft Purview return no results.

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog returns no results when auditing is off.
claims.quote: Running the **Search-UnifiedAuditLog** cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell also returns no results.

claims.claim: The Office 365 Management Activity API cannot access audit data when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the [Office 365 Management Activity API](/en-us/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference) or [Microsoft Sentinel](/en-us/azure/sentinel/overview) to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft Sentinel cannot access the organization's audit logs when auditing is off.
claims.quote: If you turn off auditing in Microsoft 365, you can't use the [Office 365 Management Activity API](/en-us/office/office-365-management-api/office-365-management-activity-api-reference) or [Microsoft Sentinel](/en-us/azure/sentinel/overview) to access auditing data or logs for your organization.

claims.claim: Audit licensing requires an appropriate organization subscription and per-user licensing to log and retain records.
claims.quote: Licensing for Audit (Standard) and Audit (Premium) requires the appropriate organization subscription that provides access to the audit log search tool and per-user licensing that's required to log and retain audit records.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: One year retention
claims.claim: One-year retention requires the activity's user to have Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5, Microsoft Purview Suite or an E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on.
claims.quote: must have an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 license or a Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) or E5 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.

claims.claim: The ten-year audit retention add-on is additional to the underlying Premium licensing.
claims.quote: In addition to the required licensing for Audit (Premium) (described in the next section), a user must be assigned a 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on license to retain their audit records for 10 years.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Logging can be off; What to check
claims.claim: Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled in Exchange Online PowerShell verifies auditing, with True indicating enabled.
claims.quote:
Get-AdminAuditLogConfig | Format-List UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled
```

A value of `True` for the *UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled* property indicates that auditing is turned on.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Logging can be off
claims.claim: The same property always returns False in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: Although the **Get-AdminAuditLogConfig** cmdlet is also available in Security & Compliance PowerShell, the *UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled* property is always `False`, even when auditing is turned on.

claims.claim: New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy supports Name, RecordTypes, RetentionDuration and Priority in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: New-UnifiedAuditLogRetentionPolicy -Name "Microsoft Teams Audit Policy" -Description "One year retention policy for all Microsoft Teams activities" -RecordTypes MicrosoftTeams -RetentionDuration TenYears -Priority 100

claims.claim: Creating retention policies requires Organization Configuration.
claims.quote: You need the *Organization Configuration* role in the Microsoft Purview portal to create or modify an audit retention policy.

claims.claim: An organization can have up to fifty audit retention policies.

claims.claim: The default audit retention policy cannot be modified.
claims.quote: Audit (Premium) in Microsoft Purview provides a default audit log retention policy for all organizations. You can't modify this policy.

claims.claim: The Dataverse audit setup path is Power Platform admin center > Security > Compliance > Auditing > environment > Set up auditing > Turn on auditing.
